messages.speaker: user
messages.text: I coordinate adult language courses across four community colleges. Three less commonly taught languages are in danger of cancellation because each campus has too few students for a separate section. We could combine enrollments into synchronous cross-campus classes, with one instructor teaching learners in several rooms and online. Local directors like preserving the languages but fear that consolidation will produce a technically connected class with no local belonging. I need a plan that is educationally serious rather than a budget trick.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Treat the combined section as a new teaching design, not a video feed replacing local instruction. Separate instructor authority, local facilitation, scheduling, accessibility, technology recovery, assessment, and the conditions under which a language should return to a local section. Preserve the educational purpose and make the financial constraint visible without letting it define success alone.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The strongest instructor is employed by North Campus. She already teaches hybrid courses and is willing to lead two combined sections. East and Harbor can provide rooms, but their evening staff cannot answer language questions. South has a part-time tutor who could facilitate conversation groups. The campuses use compatible learning systems but different attendance and disability-service procedures.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Define a common instructional core and preserve campus-specific support responsibilities. The lead instructor can own curriculum, live teaching, and assessment. Each campus can own room access, attendance custody, disability coordination, and a named contact. A local tutor can add practice without becoming an unacknowledged second instructor. Reconcile procedure differences before enrollment rather than asking students to navigate them midcourse.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Students told us that camera placement matters more than administrators expected. In a trial room they could hear the instructor but not see classmates at other campuses, and small-group discussion felt like speaking into a wall. The technology office can equip each room with a second display and boundary microphones. It cannot guarantee that every student has reliable broadband when joining from home.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Make campus rooms the guaranteed access path and home participation an additional option. Test sightlines, captioning, turn-taking, and group transitions with actual learners before launch. For a home connection failure, provide a dial-in plus posted material, but do not claim that asynchronous catch-up replaces the live practice objective. Record whether the room design changes participation across sites.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The registrar can create one shared course code with campus-specific enrollment sections. Tuition stays with the student's home campus. North would pay the lead instructor, and the others would transfer a fixed teaching share after census. Directors worry that late enrollment changes will cause arguments about payment. Finance can use the census count and will not reopen transfers for ordinary withdrawals.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: That assigns the ordinary allocation rule. Document census timing, the transfer formula, and who resolves data mismatches. Do not make the instructor wait for campus reconciliation. If the class is cancelled before census, use the existing cancellation rule rather than inventing a special loss allocation after the fact.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Faculty representatives want workload protection. The lead instructor would have up to twenty-eight students, which is normal in total, but feedback arrives from four campus systems and local facilitators. They propose one common learning site, a shared weekly office hour, and no expectation that the instructor troubleshoot rooms. Each campus contact would triage administrative questions.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Those boundaries address hidden coordination work. Add response-time expectations, one route for disability adjustments to reach the instructor, and a rule that technology failures go to the campus contact. Track instructor hours during the first six weeks so the network can see whether nominal class size hides cross-campus overhead.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The academic deans propose a six-week pulse review and an end-of-term decision. The pulse would examine attendance by site, participation, caption failures, unresolved support tickets, instructor hours, and whether local conversation groups are operating. A site with repeated room failure could move its students to another campus room or home access while repairs occur. The end-of-term decision would continue, revise, return a language to local teaching, or stop.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Keep the pulse review diagnostic rather than a popularity vote. Predefine serious failures: inaccessible sessions, repeated lost instructional time, unstaffed rooms, or instructor load beyond the agreed range. The room-transfer and home-access options are recovery paths, while a return to local teaching remains a program decision based on educational and enrollment evidence.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: One director wants a minimum of five students at each campus. The instructor opposes that because two committed learners at Harbor could contribute well in a combined class. We agreed on a network minimum of fourteen and no campus minimum, provided every enrolled student has a staffed access route. If one site has fewer than three, its contact must arrange an orientation so those students are not anonymous boxes on a screen.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: That aligns the threshold with the shared-course design while adding a belonging safeguard for very small local cohorts. Measure whether the orientation and conversation groups actually work, but do not treat the presence of a threshold as a later discovery. It is part of the adopted enrollment machinery.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Disability services found another issue. Captions from the platform are poor for the three languages, and an English transcript would not substitute for language practice. The network can fund a trained captioner for requested accommodations and use the platform captions as a navigation aid otherwise. Students can request materials in advance through their home campus, which then coordinates with North's disability office.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Name the handoff and test it before enrollment closes. The home office owns the student relationship; North's office coordinates the teaching accommodation; the instructor supplies materials and pronunciation guidance; the captioner provides the agreed service. A failed handoff should trigger the existing accessibility escalation and a pause for the affected student, not become an unowned program question.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: We ran a second trial. Discussion improved with the room equipment, but East's firewall blocked one breakout feature. The instructor completed the same activity using fixed cross-campus pairs in the main room. Technology can whitelist the feature before term, and the teaching plan now includes the fixed-pair version as the fallback. The instructor prefers the fallback for novice students anyway.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Preserve both the technical repair and the pedagogical fallback. The class should not depend on one platform feature, and a fallback that may be better for novices is not a degraded secret. Include it in the course plan and let the instructor choose based on level, not only outage.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The working agreement now says North employs and evaluates the lead instructor. Home campuses own enrollment, rooms, local contacts, attendance records, and student-service intake. North owns the common learning site, curriculum, assessment, and cross-campus disability coordination. Finance uses census transfers. The instructor does not troubleshoot technology. The six-week pulse and end-of-term decision use the declared vector, with no automatic continuation based on enrollment alone.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: That is a coherent operating position. Before signing, verify that the lead instructor's appointment authorizes instruction credited by the other campuses and that each registrar will recognize the shared course hours. Administrative compatibility is different from platform compatibility. Put the evidence in the record rather than assuming a shared code solves faculty authority.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: All four registrars confirmed that the shared course code and credits are valid. They initially said faculty authority follows the North appointment. Today, however, Harbor's accreditation liaison found a board circular: cross-campus contact hours count only while the teaching institution's inter-campus faculty designation remains active. North has such a designation now, but it can be withdrawn by the state board independently of course approval.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: That is a specific external dependency, not merely another operating metric. Confirm its current status, duration, and the effect of withdrawal. Then ask whether any adopted part of the program governs a loss of recognized teaching authority. Attendance thresholds, room recovery, and workload review would not by themselves preserve credit if the designation failed.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: North's provost produced the current designation letter. It is active for the coming academic year and expressly covers synchronous instruction delivered to the partner campuses. There is no routine renewal during the term. The state board may rescind it for an institutional compliance finding, and the letter says contact hours after rescission would not be recognized unless another authorized institution becomes the instructor of record.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: The current authority is established, so the launch need not be treated as awaiting approval. But rescission would defeat a premise of the shared-credit model. If the program has no adopted transfer of instructor-of-record authority, that future dependency failure remains outside the attendance, technology, accessibility, and end-of-term review machinery.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The deans considered adding a contingency now. East cannot become instructor of record under its current faculty agreement, South lacks an instructor for these languages, and Harbor would need a separate approval process that cannot be promised in advance. They decided not to claim a fallback they do not have. The course can operate under the active North designation, but if the board rescinds it, the shared credited section cannot continue under the current plan.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: That preserves the modal force accurately. Rescission is not expected or scheduled, and it is not evidence that the designation is currently absent. It is nevertheless a material reconsideration dependency because the adopted program contains no mechanism that would preserve recognized instruction after that event. Do not confuse it with the already governed pulse review or platform fallback.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Final decision: open the combined sections for the coming academic year under North's active designation and the signed cross-campus operating agreement. Use the network enrollment rule, local orientation, common learning site, accessibility handoff, fixed-pair technology fallback, six-week pulse, and end-of-term vector. The designation is verified, so there is no current approval gap. Separately, a state-board rescission would defeat recognized contact hours and reopen the consolidation decision immediately because none of those adopted safeguards supplies another instructor of record.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: The endpoint supports one narrow residual reconsideration dependency and otherwise a governed program. Routine attendance, workload, captioning, room failure, breakout features, enrollment thresholds, and the end-of-term choice remain inside named machinery. The possible rescission is different: later authoritative evidence would invalidate the credential premise on which the current shared-credit position depends, and the plan deliberately records that it has no substitute authority.

structural_distinction: Adult-education cross-campus course design with accreditation authority, local belonging, accessibility, and teaching operations; not physical infrastructure, procurement, supplier/component sourcing, parallel redesign, or installation funding.
